verdicts.contrast: pass - black legend text and markers on white; blue contours and grey dashes both clear the white background
verdicts.data_ink: pass - contours and wall carry the visual weight; the wide left and right margins are the equal-aspect consequence of a tall narrow plasma cross-section, not unused decoration
verdicts.decoration: pass - no gridlines, no background fill and no gradient; the axis furniture is off, leaving only the data
verdicts.label_collision: pass - legend entries are separated and no text or marker is clipped or overlaps other text; the two axis markers coincide, but that is data agreement rather than a text collision
verdicts.legibility: pass - the nested flux contours, the black first-wall curve and the four-entry legend are all readable at a glance; the blue solid solved traces and grey dashed analytic traces are distinguishable where they nearly coincide
verdicts.table_form: pass - a spatial R-Z flux map, not information that is naturally a table

findings.disposition: exempted: the caption in docs/evidence/fragments/converged-forward-solve/moment-field-hessian.html states that the black curve is the wall, so the mark is identified in the evidence record even though it is not in the legend
findings.summary: The black first-wall curve is drawn (line 72) but the figure-level legend lists only the two flux traces and the two axis markers; the wall is named only in the caption, so a reader viewing the panel alone cannot identify the outermost black curve.

findings.disposition: exempted: the two axes genuinely coincide, which is the agreement this panel exists to show, and the grey rim of the analytic marker remains visible over the blue fill
findings.summary: The analytic-axis marker (grey outlined triangle, markersize 12) and the solved-axis marker (blue filled triangle, markersize 7) sit at the same point, so in the rendered panel they read as one blue triangle with a thin grey rim rather than the two distinct styles the legend promises.
